title: The 10 Best Cordless Drills
subtitle: Ranked from live Amazon data — best-sellers, real ratings, honest trade-offs.
intro: We pulled the best-selling cordless drills on Amazon, then scored each one on a single 100-point scale built from its star rating, how many people have reviewed it, its value for the price, and its feature set. Two batteries or one, brushless or brushed, heavy-duty or grab-and-go — here is where each lands.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: DEWALT DCD771C2 20V MAX Cordless Drill/Driver Kit
products.best_for: Most homeowners: a proven drill with two batteries in the box.
products.verdict: The safe default. Nearly 50,000 reviews at 4.8 stars, two batteries in the box, and enough power for almost any home job.
pros: Most-reviewed drill here by a mile — 49,952 ratings at 4.8 stars
Two speeds (0-450 / 1500 rpm) cover both driving and drilling
Ships with two 1.3Ah batteries, so one is always charging
1/2 in ratcheting chuck grips bits tightly
cons: Brushed motor — less efficient and shorter-lived than brushless
1.3Ah packs are small; heavy use means frequent recharges

products.name: DEWALT DCD777D1 20V MAX Brushless Drill/Driver
products.best_for: Buyers who want brushless runtime and an LED on DEWALT 20V MAX.
products.verdict: The upgrade pick. Brushless motor, LED, and a bigger 2.0Ah battery on the same DEWALT platform — worth it if you want longer runtime and tool life.
pros: Brushless motor runs cooler and lasts longer
Larger 2.0Ah battery plus a built-in LED
Same 20V MAX battery platform as the rest of DEWALT's line
cons: One battery in the box, where the DCD771 ships with two
The price moves a lot ($106 to $138 between our last two checks), so check it before you buy

products.name: AVID POWER 20V Cordless Drill Set (22 accessories)
products.best_for: Light jobs at home: furniture, shelves, picture hooks, under $50.
products.verdict: The value champ. 23,000+ reviews at 4.6 stars for under $50, light in the hand, and it comes ready to work with a 22-piece bit set.
pros: 23,667 reviews at 4.6 stars — enormous trust for the price
Only 2.5 lb with a rubber grip and LED light
15+1 clutch plus a 22-piece bit set, ready out of the box
Battery has a real-time charge-level display
cons: Only accepts AVID POWER's own batteries

products.name: COMOWARE 20V Cordless Drill (34-pc bit set)
products.best_for: Occasional DIY on the tightest budget, with a big bit set included.
products.verdict: A lot of drill for about $27 — two speeds, a 25+1 clutch, and a 34-piece bit set. Fine for occasional DIY.
pros: Two variable speeds up to 1300 rpm
LED light plus a 34-piece bit set included

products.name: PULITUO 20V Cordless Drill/Driver (2 batteries)
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want two batteries so one is always charged.
products.verdict: Two batteries in the box for under $40, plus two speeds and an LED. Basic build, but a lot of kit for the money.
pros: Two speeds up to 1500 rpm, 30 Nm, 21+1 clutch

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 CMCD700C1 Cordless Drill/Driver Kit
products.best_for: Starting on CRAFTSMAN V20 with a 1/2 in chuck for larger bits.
products.verdict: A name-brand middle option on the V20 platform, with an LED and a 1/2 in chuck. Solid, if not exciting.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BDCDD12C 12V MAX Drill/Driver
products.best_for: Overhead and in-cabinet work where a 2.18 lb drill saves your wrist.
products.verdict: The featherweight. At 2.18 lb it's the easiest to hold overhead or in a cabinet — just keep the jobs light.
pros: Only 2.18 lb — lightest drill on the list

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX Drill + 100-piece Kit
products.best_for: A first toolbox: drill plus a 100-piece bit and socket set.
products.verdict: Buy it for the 100-piece bit and socket kit as much as the drill. A complete starter set for a first home toolbox.
pros: 100-piece bit and socket set included — instant starter kit
cons: 650 rpm single-speed is low on power

products.name: DEKOPRO 20V Cordless Drill Set
products.best_for: A 20V drill under $30 with an 18+1 clutch.
products.verdict: Among the cheapest 20V drills here, and it sells hard — 4,000+ bought a month. Bare-bones but gets light jobs done.

products.name: FADAKWALT 12V Cordless Drill Set
products.best_for: Flat-pack furniture and hanging shelves for under $25.
products.verdict: The budget floor. Lowest price on the list, with an LED and a bit set — fine for hanging shelves and flat-pack furniture.

avoid.name: JH Steady 21V Cordless Drill Driver Kit
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on core specs
avoid.verdict: The lowest-ranked drill we found — and the listing itself is the reason. Skip it.
reasons: The spec sheet claims a 30,000 rpm max speed while the description says 1,500 rpm. A drill does not spin at 30,000 rpm — that is a rotary-tool number. When a listing contradicts itself on the headline spec, you can't trust anything else on the page.
"JH Steady" is a no-name brand with no service record, and the battery is a proprietary 21V pack. When it dies you are buying a whole new drill, not a replacement battery.
The page sells several different "kit options" under one listing, so its ratings may not even be for this exact drill — you can't tell what the stars are actually rating.
"21V" is marketing inflation. Serious drills run 18V or 20V MAX; padding the number to 21 is a spec game, not extra power.

buyers_guide.a: 12V drills are lighter and cheaper and handle furniture, shelves, and small jobs. 20V drills have the torque for drilling into hardwood, driving long screws, and general home projects. If you only own one drill, buy 20V.

Brushless motors run cooler, last longer, and squeeze more runtime from a battery. They cost more. For occasional DIY, a brushed drill like the DCD771 is fine; if you'll use it weekly, pay up for brushless.

buyers_guide.q: How much torque do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Torque is twisting power. Under ~300 in-lbs (or ~35 Nm) is light-duty — screws and small bits. Name-brand 20V drills push well past that for drilling into wood and metal. None of these are rated for concrete or masonry.
Two batteries mean you never stop to charge. Kits like the DCD771 and PULITUO include a spare; most budget drills ship with one, so factor a second battery into the price.
The chuck holds the bit. A 3/8 in chuck fits most home bits; a 1/2 in chuck accepts larger bits and grips better for heavy drilling. Keyless chucks let you swap bits by hand.
